record.context_brief: Moments of the Minkowski question mark function
record.original_question: Let ?(x) be the Minkowski question mark function on [0, 1], defined by ?([0, a_1, a_2, a_3, ...]) = 2^(1-a_1) - 2^(1-(a_1+a_2)) + 2^(1-(a_1+a_2+a_3)) - ... for the regular continued-fraction expansion x = [0, a_1, a_2, ...]. Define rational functions Q_n(z) = B_n(z)z^(-n-1) by Q_0(z) = -1/(2z) and Q_n(z) = (1/2) sum_{j=0}^{n-1} (1/j!) (d^j/dz^j Q_{n-j-1}(-1)) (z^j - 1/z^(j+2)). Is it true that Lambda(t) = sum_{n>=0} Q_n'(-1)t^n/n! is an entire function and that int_0^infty Lambda(t)e^(-t) dt = int_0^1 x^2 d?(x)?

evidence.quote: This problem is taken from [1], where it is posed as a Conjecture with a positive answer.

The Minkowski question mark function ?(x) is defined by ?([0, a_1, a_2, a_3, ...]) = 2^(1-a_1) - 2^(1-(a_1+a_2)) + 2^(1-(a_1+a_2+a_3)) - ..., x in [0, 1], where x = [0, a_1, a_2, ...] stands for the representation of x by a regular continued fraction. Now, define the rational functions Q_n(z) = B_n(z)z^(-n-1), n >= 0, by Q_0(z) = -1/(2z), and recurrently by Q_n(z) = (1/2) sum_{j=0}^{n-1} (1/j!) * d^j/dz^j Q_{n-j-1}(-1) * (z^j - 1/z^(j+2)).
Problem 10. Is the following true? The function Lambda(t) = sum_infty n=0 Q_n'(-1)/n! t^n is an entire function, and int_0^infty Lambda(t)e^(-t) dt = int_0^1 x^2 d?(x).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let ?(x) denote the Minkowski question mark function on [0,1], defined for x = [0; a_1, a_2, a_3, ...] (regular continued fraction expansion, a_i ∈ ℕ) by
   ?(x) = 2^(1−a_1) − 2^(1−(a_1+a_2)) + 2^(1−(a_1+a_2+a_3)) − ⋯ .
Define a sequence of rational functions Q_n(z), n ≥ 0, recursively by
   Q_0(z) = −1/(2z),
   Q_n(z) = (1/2) ∑_{j=0}^{n−1} (1/j!) · [ (d^j/dz^j Q_{n−j−1})(−1) ] · ( z^j − 1/z^{j+2} ),  n ≥ 1.
Form the formal power series
   Λ(t) = ∑_{n=0}^∞ ( Q_n'(−1) / n! ) · t^n .
Prove or disprove the following statement: Λ(t) extends to an entire function of t ∈ ℂ, and
   ∫_0^∞ Λ(t) e^{−t} dt = ∫_0^1 x^2 d?(x) .
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture originates with Alkauskas's work on the dyadic period function and explicit series for moments of ?(x) (2008–2010). Searches turned up his original papers stating related results about series of rational functions, but no clear, citable subsequent resolution proving Λ(t) is entire and that its Laplace integral equals ∫_0^1 x^2 d?(x). Status appears unresolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: The Minkowski question mark function: explicit series for the dyadic period function and moments
status_evidence.snippet: Alkauskas constructs explicit rational-function series whose generating object is conjecturally entire and encodes the moments ∫_0^1 x^n d?(x).
status_evidence.claim: Original setting in which the entire-function/moment identity conjecture is posed.

status_evidence.title: The moments of Minkowski question mark function: the dyadic period function
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the dyadic period function G(z) as a Stieltjes-type transform of ?(x) and develops the framework for moment generating functions.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the analytic framework underlying the conjecture but does not establish entirety of Λ(t).
